title: DER SPIEGEL ownership and control
summary: DER SPIEGEL is a German news magazine published in Hamburg. Current sources identify three shareholder groups: the employee partnership, RM Hamburg Holding (Bertelsmann), and the Augstein heirs. Their commonly reported interests are 50.5%, 25.5% and 24%, but legal-entity capital percentages differ; those differences are flagged below.

gaps: Research cutoff: 2026-09-18. Searches for recent sales found no verified completed transaction superseding the shareholder groups confirmed in May 2026; this does not establish that no transaction occurred.

Reported group interests of 50.5%, 25.5% and 24% must not automatically be treated as exact direct capital percentages in the publisher partnership. Bertelsmann's 2025 statements list 25.25% for SPIEGEL-Verlag. The employee and heir direct partnership percentages, and any general-partner capital interest, remain unresolved.
The Rudolf Augstein GmbH shareholder list is dated 2022-01-13. Current official material corroborates the same three shareholder groups, but a newer GmbH shareholder list was not verified.
The official source confirms employee participation in leadership appointments, but current voting thresholds, veto rights and detailed appointment rules were not established.
The graph covers the magazine's publisher. The distinct operating-company arrangements for spiegel.de were not separately mapped.
Bertelsmann is reached at level three; its upstream owners and voting arrangements were not expanded.
Individual fractions within the undivided Augstein estate and the current employee-partnership membership distribution were not verified.
No Wikidata identifiers were verified from opened sources.
